speaker: richard_field
text: Thou art up the stair. Come and sit. It has been since Whitsun.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou. The first time I have sat down in this house since then.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Sit, Master Will. I have made a pottage. It has a French name, and I am not going to translate it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will eat it by whatever name it answers.

speaker: richard_field
text: My Holinshed, Will. The second volume. I see the gap every morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It's safe. A cat keeps it.

speaker: richard_field
text: That is not what a book is for.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He sleeps on it. The gap is a gap. The book is not lost.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: And your wife. Is she well? I ask as one householder asks after another.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: She is well. The house is in her hands while I am here.

speaker: richard_field
text: Now the town. Street by street. Who was burned out, who has rebuilt, and whether thy father's tan-yard smells as it did.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The north end. About twenty houses, and the barns with them. Tuesday the fifteenth of July. Some of it is up again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The tan-yard smells as a tan-yard smells. I have not been told it has changed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sadler's cousin lost a malt-barn. In August I raised a frame toward it.

speaker: richard_field
text: And the chapel end. What stands there.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The chapel end goes on. The great house by the chapel went by in the saying of it.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: The bowl will go cold while you count houses that are not on this table.

speaker: richard_field
text: I looked up. I am not asking. Thou hast given me the streets, and the book is the grievance I came in with.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The book is under a cloth at Mistress Ansell's. The cat is the keeper. I will bring it when I am not in the middle of a Sunday.

speaker: richard_field
text: Bring it before the gap becomes a habit. A shelf should not preach at a man every morning.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: He enjoys the preaching. I have heard it. You need not hear it twice in one dinner.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Once is enough. The book is safe, Richard. I am not careless with it.

speaker: richard_field
text: Safe is a word for a box. A book wants a hand on it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It shall have a hand. Not this afternoon.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Then eat. The herb will not wait on a chronicle.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am eating. The bells were in the street all the way here, and they will still be going at four.

speaker: richard_field
text: Thou on the stair, and a cat on my second volume. I will take the visit and forgive the cat till I see the book.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Forgive him over the bowl. That is what the bowl is for.
